question: The radius of a spherical balloon increases from 5 cm to 10 cm when more air is added to it. What is the ratio of the volume of the original balloon and the volume of the inflated balloon?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The volume of a sphere is directly proportional to the cube of its radius (V ∝ r³).

Ratio of radii = r₁ : r₂ = 5 : 10 = 1 : 2

Ratio of volumes = (r₁)³ : (r₂)³ = (1)³ : (2)³

Ratio of volumes = 1 : 8

**∴ The correct answer is 1 : 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial radius of the spherical balloon (r₁) = 5 cm

Final radius of the inflated balloon (r₂) = 10 cm

 
 
 
• 
 5 cm
 Original

 
 
 
• 
 10 cm
 Inflated

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a sphere (V) = (4 ÷ 3) × π × r³

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume of original balloon (V₁) = (4 ÷ 3) × π × (5)³

⇒ V₁ = (4 ÷ 3) × π × 125

⇒ Volume of inflated balloon (V₂) = (4 ÷ 3) × π × (10)³

⇒ V₂ = (4 ÷ 3) × π × 1000

⇒ Ratio of volumes = V₁ : V₂

⇒ Ratio = [(4 ÷ 3) × π × 125] : [(4 ÷ 3) × π × 1000]

⇒ Ratio = 125 : 1000

⇒ Ratio = 1 : 8

**∴ The correct answer is 1 : 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Surface Area of a Sphere

The total surface area of a sphere is directly proportional to the square of its radius. Formula: TSA = 4 × π × r².

Hemisphere Properties

A hemisphere is exactly half of a sphere. Its volume is V = (2 ÷ 3) × π × r³, curved surface area is CSA = 2 × π × r², and total surface area is TSA = 3 × π × r².

Scaling Ratio Rule

If the radius (or any 1D measure) of a three-dimensional object increases by a factor of **n**, its surface area increases by a factor of **n²** and its volume increases by a factor of **n³**.
